key_insight: Post-selection and entanglement are separate resources: post-selection can boost CHSH weak values, but entanglement is required to surpass the separable pre/post-selected bounds.
engineering_relevance: The results support hybrid quantum protocols that exploit weak values and post-selection for stronger nonlocal-correlation signals, with potential use in sensing, amplification, and entanglement diagnostics.
method: Analyze anomalous weak values of the CHSH operator in pre- and post-selected ensembles.
Compare three boundary-condition regimes: unrestricted, one separable boundary state, and both boundary states separable.
Optimize first over measurements for a fixed Bell operator, then over all CHSH operators to obtain maximal bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytic derivations showing that the gap beyond the separable bound tracks concurrence, and it constructs a state-adapted protocol that detects every pure two-qubit state with nonzero concurrence.
watch_item: The strongest witness performance is obtained in an ideal state-adapted setting, so practical deployment will be sensitive to state-preparation and post-selection errors.
paper_title: Quantum nonlocal correlations of anomalous weak values
